results.title: Prosecution closes case against Wontumi; court sets December 17 deadline for defence
results.content: The Accra High Court has directed former Ashanti Regional New Patriotic Party (NPP) Chairman, Bernard Antwi-Boasiako, popularly known as Chairman Wontumi, to file a submission of no case to answer by December 17, 2026, following the closure of the prosecution’s case in the Tano Nimiri illegal mining trial.

results.title: Vice President urges MTN to improve network quality and expand rural connectivity
results.content: Vice President Professor Naana Jane Opoku-Agyemang has urged MTN Ghana to increase investment in network quality, customer experience and connectivity in underserved communities as the country works to widen access to digital services. She said sustained investment in telecommunications infrastructure was critical to ensuring that more Ghanaians benefit from opportunities in the country's growing digital economy. Speaking at the MTN Ghana @30 Stakeholders Dinner in Accra, Professor Opoku-Agyemang said access to reliable and affordable connectivity should not depend on where a person lives. She disclosed that the government had allocated GH¢45 million in the 2027 Budget for rural telephony projects to extend telecommunications services to communities with limited access.

results.title: Can Ghana reclaim its eco-friendly roots with the ‘takeaway’ ban?
results.content: On May 25, 2026, Ghana’s Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) issued a definitive policy directive that promises to reshape the daily routines of millions: effective January 1, 2027, the production, importation, sale, distribution, and use of expanded polystyrene foam products, universally known across West Africa as Styrofoam or 'takeaway packs,' will be illegal.

results.title: Vice President urges stronger cybersecurity to protect mobile money users
results.content: Vice President Professor Naana Jane Opoku-Agyemang has called for stronger data protection, cybersecurity and accountability in Ghana’s digital financial services sector to safeguard mobile money users against fraud and other risks. She said the rapid growth of mobile money and other digital financial services must be matched with reliable security systems to sustain public confidence in electronic transactions. Speaking at the MTN Ghana @30 Stakeholders Dinner in Accra, Professor Opoku-Agyemang acknowledged the role of mobile money in expanding financial inclusion, particularly for small businesses, families and people previously underserved by traditional banking services. She said the service had made it easier for businesses to receive payments and for families to transfer money across the country without relying on costly financial infrastructure.

results.title: Government allocates GH¢45m to expand rural telephony in 2027
results.content: Government has allocated GH¢45 million in the 2027 Budget to expand rural telephony and improve access to reliable and affordable telecommunications services in underserved communities, Vice President Professor Naana Jane Opoku-Agyemang has announced. She said the investment forms part of efforts to bridge Ghana’s digital divide and ensure that communities outside major urban centres benefit from the country's growing digital economy. Speaking at the MTN Ghana @30 Stakeholders Dinner in Accra, the Vice President stressed that access to technology should not depend on where a person lives. "Our priority is to extend reliable and affordable connectivity to communities that remain underserved, while upgrading existing infrastructure to support digital services," she said.

results.title: Mahama targets 30% cross-border electricity trade in West Africa within five years
results.content: President John Mahama has called for greater investment in connecting national electricity grids across West Africa, saying it could raise cross-border power trade from the current 7 per cent to nearly 30 per cent within five years.

results.title: Local organic fertiliser offers farmers a pathway to climate-resilient agriculture
results.content: As changing weather patterns, declining soil fertility and rising input costs threaten agricultural livelihoods, farmers in Ashanti and the Northern Region are turning to Organic Farming Aid. Their experiences offer insights into a possible response to climate pressures, but questions remain about the evidence, affordability and potential for wider adoption.

results.title: The NDC doesn’t have a First Vice or a Second Vice
results.content: There is a need to set the records straight about the positions of Regional Vice-Chairmen in the National Democratic Congress (NDC). This is not about personalities, political interests or internal factions. It is about what the party’s constitution actually says. A careful reading of the 2014 NDC Constitution, Article 20(1)(b), makes provision for Two Vice-Chairmen as members of the Regional Executive Committee. More importantly, Article 20(2)(b) again provides for the election of Two Vice-Chairmen by the Regional Party Conference. The language of the Constitution is clear. It establishes two positions of Regional Vice-Chairman. It does not expressly establish a hierarchy of First Regional Vice-Chairman and Second Regional Vice-Chairman. results.title: From a house to an iPad, Ghanaians reveal who they want to surprise this Christmas
results.content: With Christmas approaching, some Ghanaians are already thinking about how to make the festive season special for the people who have supported and stood by them throughout the year. For some, the planned gifts are big-ticket items, including a house and a G-Wagon. Others are considering gadgets, bicycles and jewellery as ways of expressing love and appreciation. In a series of responses, five people shared who they hope to surprise this Christmas, why they have chosen them and what they intend to give. Ama Poniwaaa says she hopes to surprise her boyfriend with a house and a G-Wagon, describing him as someone who holds a special place in her life. “You don't know how much this guy means to me. He's so dear to my heart. I wish to give him the whole world,” she said.

results.title: Vigilantism, brutalisation not the right way for South Africa to address migration crisis – Mahama
results.content: President John Mahama says migration challenges cannot be resolved through vigilantism, condemning attacks on foreign nationals in South Africa.

He said Parliament had granted the MP leave of absence, arguing that the circumstances preventing him from attending sittings did not amount to an unexplained absence.
